svg.title: A 4-year-old tells the nurse that his stuffed rabbit gets sad when left alone and needs a blanket at night. His mother reports that when he accidentally broke a toy last week, he cried and said he was 'a bad boy.'
svg.desc: Animism is the preoperational belief that inanimate objects have life and feelings, a developmentally normal pattern at this age and not a sign of a thought disorder; object permanence is an infant task and conservation does not emerge until concrete operational thinking in the school-age years. Erikson's initiative vs. guilt describes the preschooler whose ambitions and exploration outrun ability, so a failure like breaking a toy easily triggers guilt, while trust vs. mistrust belongs to infancy and industry vs. inferiority belongs to the school-age stage.
